registeredBy: Drafted under Sam's signal standard (2026-11-06), Phase 4 of the seven-groups plan; registered before any run
hypothesis: In a country with no state-based armed conflict this year (UCDP/PRIO), a year with an unrest spike episode (protests or violence as a share of the country's GDELT events at 3 or more standard deviations above its own previous 24 months) is followed by armed conflict located in the country the next calendar year more often than quiet country-years in general.
knownLimits: UCDP's yearly files only: the outcome is armed conflict (25 or more battle deaths in the year) located in the country the next calendar year, not within 3 months as the plan first said. A monthly test would need the UCDP event dataset (GED), not on disk.

GDELT 1.0 months on disk start in 2016 (npm run gdelt:daily), so with a 24-month baseline the first year scored is 2018 and the last is the year before the latest UCDP year: about seven years, all of them recent.

The base rate is pooled over every quiet country-year in the sample, since onsets are too rare for a rate per country. Countries differ a great deal in how likely conflict is, so a pass can partly reflect which countries have spikes.
A conflict that was active in earlier years, paused for a year and restarted counts as an onset.
GDELT codes events from news reports by machine; coverage and coding errors vary by country and year. Shares are used, not counts, since volume grew many times over.
